section_summary: This section begins with the end of a study of Japan’s major fishing and whaling companies, followed by correspondence about Japanese fisheries and a concentrated debate over a proposed 1947–48 Antarctic whaling expedition. British, New Zealand and Australian objections are weighed against SCAP’s arguments about food, oil and foreign exchange, with memoranda addressing conservation, reparations and SCAP’s legal authority. The section ends with an attached Far Eastern Commission policy proposal and the opening page of a consultation record.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Big Fishing Companies
subfiles.about: Profiles major Japanese fishing and whaling companies, their ownership, fleets, facilities and wartime losses.
subfiles.summary: The surviving portion of Preliminary Study No. 5 profiles Nichiro, Taiyo and Kyokuyo, listing officers, shareholders, subsidiaries, vessels, processing capacity and production. It describes the loss of overseas fishing grounds and whaling ships, and ends with a distribution list.

subfiles.title: Letter on Natural Resources Section fisheries reports
subfiles.about: Thanks Greaves for fisheries reports useful to U.S. policy formulation.
subfiles.summary: Flory says the reports help address gaps in factual information about Japanese fisheries.

subfiles.title: British attitude toward continuation of Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Records Everson’s view that Britain opposed further Japanese Antarctic whaling.
subfiles.summary: Everson cites the catch limit and inefficient Japanese processing. He supports expanding Japanese fishing through bilateral agreements and suggests separating fishing policy from whaling.

subfiles.title: Reply to Montgomery Phister on fisheries consultation
subfiles.about: Offers to discuss Japanese fisheries questions with Phister’s committee.
subfiles.summary: Flory welcomes consultation with the fishing industry at its next committee meeting.

subfiles.title: Letter proposing discussion of the Japanese problem
subfiles.about: Suggests discussing Japanese fisheries at the committee’s next meeting.
subfiles.summary: Phister says the Japanese problem may become important.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram 100 on expanding Japanese fishing grounds
subfiles.about: Requests Soviet concurrence for temporary Japanese fishing off Kamchatka.
subfiles.summary: SCAP identifies underused trawling and salmon grounds off Kamchatka, estimates the vessels and output for proposed expeditions, and reports agreements concerning the Yellow and East China seas.

subfiles.title: British aide-mémoire opposing renewed Japanese Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: Urges a halt to Japanese Antarctic whaling and reparations allocation of its factory ships.
subfiles.summary: Britain argues that other nations can reach the catch ceiling, Japanese processing yields less product, and Japan’s past whaling practices endangered whale stocks. It asks for a report on the recent expedition and the whale oil allocated to Germany.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram 107 proposing a second Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Seeks an urgent decision on a three-factory-ship expedition for 1947–48.
subfiles.summary: SCAP cites Japan’s shortage of protein and edible oils, gives planned vessels, supplies, schedule and projected production, and asks Washington to consult interested governments promptly.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation on Japanese vessels and reparations
subfiles.about: Discusses whether large fishing and whaling vessels should receive a specific reparations exemption.
subfiles.summary: Flory favors reliance on a general SCAP retention provision because a specific fisheries exemption would reopen contentious Far Eastern Commission debates.

subfiles.title: Draft language on Antarctic whale oil distribution
subfiles.about: Supplies figures and allocation language for a reply to Britain.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reports 12,200 metric tons of whale oil from the 1946–47 expedition, discusses proposed allocations to Japan and Germany, and gives other production and catch figures.

subfiles.title: New Zealand aide-mémoire on Japanese pelagic whaling
subfiles.about: Opposes further Japanese Antarctic whaling and urges reparations treatment of whaling vessels.
subfiles.summary: New Zealand says its acceptance of the prior expedition was limited to an emergency season and argues that future Japanese participation would reduce oil yield and preserve vessels with military potential.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on 1946–47 Antarctic whale-catch statistics
subfiles.about: Transmits corrected catch statistics for the Hashidate Maru and Nisshin Maru fleets.
subfiles.summary: The airgram gives whale counts by species and revised weekly blue-whale-unit totals for transmission to the international statistics bureau in Sandefjord.

subfiles.title: Australian statement opposing further Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Restates opposition to further expeditions pending a peace settlement.
subfiles.summary: Australia invokes prior U.S. assurances and again seeks reparations allocation of Japanese whaling equipment.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on Allied Council consideration of whaling
subfiles.about: Asks whether Washington objects to placing the proposed expedition before the Allied Council.
subfiles.summary: The corrected copy notes an erroneous Seoul dateline in the original processing.

subfiles.title: Erroneously processed copy of Allied Council telegram
subfiles.about: Duplicates the Allied Council inquiry under an erroneous Seoul dateline.
subfiles.summary: Original processing copy of the telegram corrected on page 419.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on 1947–48 Antarctic whaling and conservation
subfiles.about: Warns that forcing acceptance of a Japanese catch could undermine whaling cooperation.
subfiles.summary: Flory recommends protecting the cooperative catch limit and whale stocks.

subfiles.title: Suggested points for replying to the British whaling aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: Outlines possible rebuttals to British objections to a second expedition.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum discusses catch limits, inspection, accession to whaling agreements, reparations and security. It flags diplomatic difficulty over SCAP’s proposed third factory ship.

subfiles.title: Recommendation against a 1947–48 Japanese Antarctic expedition
subfiles.about: Recommends against authorizing a second expedition despite its expected economic benefits.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum weighs food and foreign-exchange gains against objections from whaling partners, risks to the catch ceiling, and likely opposition in the Far Eastern Commission. It recommends requesting meat and oil from Allied catches for Japan.

subfiles.title: European Affairs view on the proposed whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Opposes authorizing a Japanese expedition in the face of Allied objections.
subfiles.summary: Hickerson argues that Japanese participation cannot increase the permitted total catch and would damage confidence in U.S. policy.

subfiles.title: Draft telegram declining the proposed Antarctic expedition
subfiles.about: Drafts instructions explaining why Washington cannot authorize another expedition.
subfiles.summary: The draft cites categorical British, Australian and New Zealand opposition, conservation commitments and reparations issues. It says the United States would oppose unjustified permanent restrictions on Japanese whaling.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram 128 asking for a reply
subfiles.about: Asks when Washington will answer the Allied Council inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo requests a prompt reply to its earlier whaling telegram.

subfiles.title: Fragmentary incoming telegram on Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Concerns the pending decision on Japanese whaling; much of the OCR is illegible.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary telegram concerning a decision on the whaling question.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram 132 urging a second expedition
subfiles.about: Presses Washington to permit the 1947–48 expedition despite Allied objections.
subfiles.summary: SCAP emphasizes food, foreign exchange and occupation costs, disputes accusations of waste, and promises compliance with whaling rules. It proposes a compromise requiring Far Eastern Commission approval for any later expedition.

subfiles.title: New Zealand objections to Japanese whaling operations
subfiles.about: Forwards a New Zealand newspaper editorial on Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: The despatch reports local press reaction and encloses an editorial from The Dominion, which raises royalty and espionage concerns.

subfiles.title: Authority of SCAP to direct an Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Assesses SCAP’s authority relative to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Snow reviews surrender and occupation instruments and concludes that SCAP may order another expedition absent a contrary Commission policy. He also describes an urgent U.S. interim directive as a possible route.

subfiles.title: Proposed policy on Japanese fishing, whaling and pearl fishing
subfiles.from: Australian representative to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Proposes fishing boundaries, restrictions on pelagic whaling and reparations provisions.
subfiles.summary: Pages 442–444 have no legible OCR. The surviving proposal calls for use of Japanese fishing resources within a defined area, Commission approval for extensions, and restrictions on whaling outside that area. It also addresses pearl fishing and removal of vessels and equipment as reparations.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission circulation note
subfiles.about: Circulates the Australian fishing, whaling and pearl-fishing proposal.
subfiles.summary: Refers the proposal to Committee No. 2 on Economic and Financial Affairs.

subfiles.title: Consultation on the 1947–48 Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition
subfiles.about: Records the opening of a consultation with British, New Zealand, Australian and Norwegian representatives.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring explains the proposed SCAP expedition’s occupation benefits and pledges compliance with whaling agreements; the record continues beyond this section.
